content: Folic acid injection can be administered via intramuscular (IM), intravenous (IV), or subcutaneous (SC) routes in cases of exceptionally severe disease or when gastrointestinal absorption is impaired or known to be compromised. In resistant cases, higher doses may be required. The standard dosage is 1 mg per day. Patients should be closely monitored, and the maintenance dose should be adjusted if signs of relapse become apparent. In conditions such as alcoholism, hemolytic anemia, anticonvulsant therapy, or chronic infection, the maintenance dose may need to be increased. Parenteral drug products should always be visually inspected for particulate matter and discoloration prior to administration, provided the solution and container allow for such inspection. Research indicates that patients with impaired kidney function, including premature neonates, who receive parenteral aluminum at levels exceeding 4 to 5 mcg/kg/day, may accumulate aluminum to levels associated with central nervous system and bone toxicity. Tissue loading of aluminum may occur even at lower administration rates. Folic acid alone is not an appropriate treatment for pernicious anemia or other megaloblastic anemias caused by Vitamin B12 deficiency. This product contains benzyl alcohol, which has been associated with a fatal condition known as Gasping Syndrome in premature infants. A daily dose of 1 mg of folic acid may obscure the diagnosis of pernicious anemia, as hematologic remission can occur while neurological symptoms continue to progress. Folic acid is a complex organic compound found in liver, yeast, and other substances, and it can also be synthesized. It appears as a yellow or yellowish-orange, odorless crystalline powder. It is very slightly soluble in water, insoluble in alcohol, chloroform, and ether, but readily dissolves in dilute solutions of alkali hydroxides and carbonates. It should be protected from light, and the vial should remain in its carton until its contents are used. Folic Acid Injection, USP, is available in a concentration of 5 mg/mL for IM, IV, or SC use. It is supplied in 10 mL multiple-dose vials and is available by prescription only.
